meta.title: Tess and the Cloud Machine
meta.teaser: Help a town mender free a cloud and bring back the kite-fair breeze!

text: You are drawing plans for the town kite fair.
TAP! A paper pinwheel lands at your window.
Mom looks up. "Shall we see what that is?"

commands.response: Your plans show a kite with seven tails. Mom suggests starting with one.
Little clouds still bob upside down above the houses.
Little clouds are bobbing upside down! A paper pinwheel taps the glass.
The window is open. The pinwheel carries a folded note.
You open the low window with Mom. The pinwheel drops a note onto the sill.
LOOK WINDOW first. What is tapping the glass?
The note says: Please visit my WORKSHOP. The cloud machine has hiccups! - Tess. Mom walks outside with you.
Your plans are safe on the desk. You leave them there for later.
The window belongs in the wall. It would make a very awkward hat.
Your kite plans unfold across the desk. One tail looks like a noodle.
The note says: Please visit my WORKSHOP. The cloud machine has hiccups! - Tess.
The note is outside. LOOK WINDOW, then OPEN WINDOW to bring it in.
A note from Tess is folded into the pinwheel. TAKE NOTE to read it with Mom.
There is no note inside yet. Try looking at the window.
You cannot reach the note yet. LOOK WINDOW, then OPEN WINDOW.

default: The paper pinwheel taps softly.
Mom studies your seven-tailed kite.
A pencil rolls across your plans.
The room smells of fresh crayons.
hints: What is tapping the window?
LOOK WINDOW, then OPEN WINDOW with Mom.
LOOK WINDOW, OPEN WINDOW, then TAKE NOTE.

text: You and Mom step outside.
Cloud fluff rolls along the street like cotton balls.
A cat is wearing a tiny cloud hat.

commands.response: Soft bits of cloud roll past. One looks exactly like a potato.
The orange cat blinks under its fluffy hat. It seems quite pleased.
The cat says Mrrp. Perhaps that means: Do you like my new hat?
Tess has a ground-floor workshop at the end of the garden path.
Tess asked you to visit her WORKSHOP. Mom can walk there with you.
You and Mom follow the path to Tess. Her workshop bell rings: DING!
You tell the fluff to sit. It rolls over instead. Almost!
You call toward the workshop. A bell gives a little ding.
The fluff drifts away. The workshop is a better place to start.
You pause beside the cat. It gives you a very important sniff.
You check your shoes. Both still there. Excellent.

default: A bit of fluff rolls into a flowerpot.
The cat adjusts its cloud hat.
The workshop bell gives a tiny ding.
Mom points along the garden path.
hints: Tess asked you to come to her workshop.
The workshop is at the end of the garden path.
GO WORKSHOP.

text: Tess the town mender waits in her workshop.
Her yellow apron is full of pencils.
Outside, a small cloud makes enormous sneezes.

commands.response: Tess says: We need the guide at the library. Take the long TONGS and come with me.
Tess says: Puff is stuck in my cloud machine! We need its picture guide. Will you help me work out a repair?
Cloud hats float above the park. One has landed on a statue.
Tess wears a yellow work apron. There are three pencils behind one ear.
Long wooden tongs for reaching things. They open and close with a gentle squeeze.
Your note brought you to the workshop. Tess is ready to explain the problem.
You return Tess her note. She folds it into a smaller pinwheel and thanks you.
Tess lends you the TONGS and leads you to the park. Mom will meet you both at the kite fair.
Tess says: TALK TESS first, so we can make a plan together.
Tess is a person, not a tool. She offers to walk with you instead.
The city is much too big for your pockets. Even the extra pocket.
You say hello to the tongs. Their wooden tips clap politely.
You call GOOD MORNING, CITY! A baker waves a floury hand.

default: Tess finds another pencil in her apron.
A pinwheel turns very slowly.
Something outside gives a tiny sneeze.
The tongs rest on the workbench.
hints: Tess needs a helper. Ask about her plan.
TALK TESS before taking the long tool.
TALK TESS, then TAKE TONGS.

text: Tess walks with you through the park.
Bea the gardener catches tumbling flowerpots.
A watering can floats past. This weather is very mixed up!

commands.response: Bea says: You have the tool-room key. The guide is in the LIBRARY.
Bea points under the bench. The tool-room KEY is still there.
Bea says: A gust blew the tool-room KEY under this bench. You may borrow it with Tess.
The bench is empty underneath now. The key is in your bag.
A brass key lies beneath the bench. Its tag shows a little cloud.
Bea steadies the bench with her boot. She looks as though she knows this park well.
You already have the brass key.
You pick up the tool-room key. Its cloud tag jingles against your fingers.
The sign says: LIBRARY. There is a helpful arrow and a drawing of a book.
Bea has muddy boots and a very large sunhat. She is ready to help.
You and Tess follow the sign to the library, carrying the tool-room key.
The tool room is locked. Ask Bea about its key before you leave.
Bea laughs. She is staying here to catch her flowerpots.
The bench is bolted down. It has no plans to travel today.
The sign needs to stay here so everyone can find the library.
The bench says nothing. It is saving all its energy for sitting.
The sign has just one story: LIBRARY THIS WAY.
You ask the key a question. Jingle! A short but cheerful answer.
You sit beside Bea for a moment. Tess catches a drifting flowerpot.
You walk over to the sign. Its arrow points toward the library.
You can TAKE KEY once Bea shows you where it is.
Your brass key has a cloud-shaped tag. It opens the library tool room.
The key is under the bench, just where Bea pointed.
You do not see a key yet. TALK BEA for a clue.
The library has wide windows and a door shaped like an open book.
Tess asked for your help. Now you are finding the repair guide together.
Your long tongs open and close. Handy for things just out of reach.
Tess gently lowers the tongs. Tools are for objects, not for grabbing people.
You pick a leaf off the bench with the tongs. Bea gives you a grateful nod.
TALK BEA first. She knows where the key landed.

default: Bea catches one more flowerpot.
A cloud hat settles on the sign.
Tess puts a watering can back down.
A duck looks offended by the unusual weather.
hints: Bea knows where things land in this park.
TALK BEA to learn where the key fell.
TALK BEA, TAKE KEY, then GO LIBRARY.

text: The library smells of paper and fresh tea.
A little reading light shines on one shelf.
Tess says the cloud machine guide should be here.

commands.response: The reading light shines on the gap where you found the book.
Cloud Care is waiting on the shelf. TAKE BOOK to borrow it.
The picture guide is called Cloud Care. Its cover shows a smiling cloud and a gear.
Cloud Care is already in your bag.
You borrow Cloud Care. Tess opens the library lending book and signs for it.
LOOK SHELF first to find the right book among all these titles.
The guide says: Find the bent gear tooth. Stop the machine with a grown-up. Tap the tooth gently with a wooden mallet.
You read: Find the bent gear tooth. Have a grown-up stop the machine. Tap the tooth gently with a wooden mallet.
TAKE BOOK before you try to open it.
The tool-room door is locked. Its keyhole is shaped like a tiny cloud.
Tess checks the safety steps with you. The key turns, and you both walk down to the tool room. She hangs the key by the door.
The key fits. Tess says: First OPEN BOOK so we know the safe repair steps.
The shelf is staying put. You straighten one crooked book instead.
The door will not fit in your bag. Luckily, you only need to open it.
This shelf has no doors. Its books are already out in the open.
Cloud Care is a picture guide. OPEN BOOK to read the repair steps.
A book about clouds sits among books about kites and very serious umbrellas.
Tess checks the safety steps with you. The key turns, and you both walk down to the tool room. She hangs the key by the door.
The key fits. Tess says: First OPEN BOOK so we know the safe repair steps.
The brass key has the same cloud shape as the tool-room lock.
The tongs can reach high things. They are not a substitute for reading.
The note is folded neatly. The pinwheel delivery was a good idea.
There is no lock on the shelf. Try the door after reading the guide.
The tongs cannot open a locked door. Read the guide, then use the key.
Books open with your hands. This key is for the tool-room door.

default: A page rustles in the breeze.
The reading light makes a warm circle.
A librarian stamps a book: THUMP.
Tess reminds you to use your library voice.
hints: Which book might explain the cloud machine?
LOOK SHELF, TAKE BOOK, then OPEN BOOK before trying the door.
LOOK SHELF, TAKE BOOK, OPEN BOOK, then OPEN DOOR!

text: The library tool room is neat and bright.
An ice pad and a wooden mallet sit on a table.
A model cloud machine has a gear under a clear cover.

commands.response: The ice pad is safely tucked in its blue sleeve in your bag.
An ice pad in a blue sleeve. The label says: COOL HOT HANDLES. Tess has an insulated mitt to help.
You have a small wooden mallet. It is for gentle taps, not big swings.
A wooden mallet with a soft head. Tess says it will not scratch the gear.
The model shows a bent gear tooth painted blue. Just like the repair guide!
A service tunnel leads to the cloud tower. Tess knows the path.
You already packed the ice pad.
You pack the ice pad in its blue sleeve. Tess checks that it is ready.
The wooden mallet is already in your bag.
Tess shows you how to hold the little mallet. You pack it carefully.
This gear is part of the teaching model. You leave it under its cover.
With ICE and MALLET packed, you follow Tess into the service tunnel.
Tess checks the list: TAKE ICE and TAKE MALLET before we go.
You cannot pack a tunnel. You would need a very long bag.
The model is right in front of you. LOOK GEAR to study its bent tooth.
You can TAKE MALLET and carry it with you.
You can TAKE ICE and put the cooling pad in your bag.
You look all around the room. A stool seems to be looking back.
The model gear stays under its clear cover. The tongs cannot reach it.
Tess points to the cover. We study this model; the real repair is at the tower.
The tongs have soft wooden tips. They can reach without scratching.
Tess smiles at her pinwheel note. Next time she might try a paper boat.
Cloud Care shows the blue gear tooth and the stop lever. You know what to look for.

default: A tidy row of tools gleams.
Tess checks her insulated mitt.
The model cloud machine sits under its cover.
A stool creaks as though it has an opinion.
hints: Pack the things on the repair list.
TAKE ICE for hot handles and TAKE MALLET for the gear.
TAKE ICE, TAKE MALLET, then GO TUNNEL.

text: You and Tess enter the service tunnel.
A lamp hangs above the path.
A pipe goes plink, plink, plink.

commands.response: The lamp is on. Its warm glow lights the whole path.
The lamp has a pull loop, just above your reach.
A bridge waits ahead. You need light before walking farther.
The lamp is already on. Leave its loop alone for now.
You reach the lamp loop with the TONGS and pull gently. CLICK! Tess checks that the path is clear.
With the lamp on, you and Tess walk along the tunnel to the bridge.
Tess says: Let us turn on the lamp before walking farther.
The lamp is up high. A long tool could reach its loop.
The tongs are long enough to reach the lamp loop.
The ice pad will cool a hot handle later. Keep it packed.
The wooden mallet is for the repair at the tower.
Tess shakes her head gently. Use a reaching tool, not a mallet, for the lamp.
The folded note is safe in your pocket.
The pictures in Cloud Care are easier to read with a lamp on.

default: A pipe goes plink, plink.
Tess checks the path ahead.
A distant sneeze echoes through the pipe.
Your shoes make soft taps on the floor.
hints: The lamp loop is a little too high.
Use your long TONGS to reach the LAMP.
TONGS LAMP, then GO BRIDGE.

text: A sturdy footbridge crosses the water channel.
Cloud drawings decorate the wall.
You hear a faraway sneeze: AHHH-CHOO!

commands.response: A drawing shows a cloud going into the tower, then a gentle breeze coming out.
The bridge has firm boards and a sturdy railing. Tess checks it before you cross.
The cloud tower is beyond the bridge, at the end of the service path.
No need to climb. You can see the tower drawing from down here.
You cross the sturdy bridge with Tess and step out beside the cloud tower.
Use the walkway and hold the railing. The bridge is for crossing, not climbing.
The tower is farther along the path. GO BRIDGE first.
That is a wall. The bridge is the way across.
Cross the bridge first to reach the tower.
You use the tongs to pick a fallen leaf off the path. Clear walkway!
This wall does not need tapping. Save the mallet for the bent gear tooth.
The cooling pad rests in its sleeve. It will be useful for a hot handle.
The mallet is for a gentle tap after Tess stops the machine.
The tongs fold neatly into your bag.
Tess points toward the tower. Your team is getting closer.
The guide shows where to find the gear. First, cross the bridge.

default: Water gurgles beneath the bridge.
The cloud drawings have very silly faces.
Tess points toward the tower.
A distant sneeze makes a pipe hum.
hints: The walkway leads to the cloud tower.
Tess has checked the bridge. Walk across together.
GO BRIDGE.

text: The cloud tower looks like a giant teapot.
A weather cart waits beside its door.
Tess warns that the busy machine has made the door handle hot.

commands.response: The weather cart holds umbrellas, empty buckets, and one enormous rain boot.
Warm air from the machine has heated the handle. Tess says not to touch it yet.
The tower has a spout like a teapot. Puff sneezes a rainbow out of it.
With her mitt, Tess helps you press the ICE pad to the handle. It cools. You open the door and leave the pad there.
The handle is too hot. Tess says to cool it before opening the door.
The path into the tower goes through its door.
You check the cart. No clouds in there. Just a very surprised umbrella.
Tess says: The handle needs cooling, not tapping. What feels cold?
The tongs cannot cool the hot handle. Look for something cold in your bag.
The ICE pad cools warm handles. Tess can help you use it safely.
The wooden mallet is for the gear, once the machine has stopped.
Your tongs are a reaching tool, not a cooling tool.
You remember the note about hiccups. That was one enormous hiccup!
Cloud Care says to make the path safe before starting a repair.

default: A rainbow puffs from the tower spout.
The cart umbrella turns inside out.
Tess checks the hot handle from a safe distance.
Puff sneezes. The rain boot wobbles.
hints: The handle needs cooling before you touch it.
The ICE pad is made for hot handles. Tess will help.
ICE DOOR.

text: The tower steps fold away like a fan.
A high latch controls the steps.
Tess waits beside the stair locks.

commands.response: The steps are unfolded and locked in place. Tess has checked them.
The folded steps have a pull latch above your reach.
The steps are already down. Tess says they are ready to climb.
You pull the high latch with the TONGS. The steps unfold. Tess locks them firmly and checks each one.
You climb the safe steps with Tess. At the top, a cloud gives a very tired sigh.
Wait until the steps are unfolded and Tess has checked their locks.
Tongs are not a ladder. Use them to reach the stair latch instead.
The tongs can reach that high latch without any climbing.
The stairs need their latch pulled, not a tap. Try the long tongs.
Keep the mallet for the gear at the top.
Tess says: One safe step at a time. You nod.
The guide shows a stop lever beside the gear. You will need both clues.

default: Puff sighs somewhere above.
The stair hinges are shaped like little fans.
Tess looks at the latch.
A little breeze ruffles your hair.
hints: The folded stairs have a latch up high.
Use the TONGS to pull the stair latch.
TONGS STAIRS, then CLIMB STAIRS.

text: Puff is wedged inside the cloud machine.
He eyes a bent GEAR with a very gloomy face.
Tess waits by the stop lever.

commands.response: Puff is a grumpy little cloud, squashed into a glass chamber. He wants room to stretch.
The bent tooth is painted blue. Keep that spot in mind.
You spot a bent blue tooth on the GEAR, just like the picture in Cloud Care.
Tess has stopped and locked the machine. She is ready to help with the gentle tap.
Tess stops the machine and locks its crank. Nothing can turn now. She says: Find the blue tooth, then tap it gently.
Puff sighs: I only wanted to make one nice breeze. Now I am all scrunched up!
Tess watches the controls. She is here to help you work safely.
The wooden mallet has a soft head. One careful tap should do.
Tess steadies the stopped gear. You tap its blue tooth with the MALLET. Click! The hatch opens. Tess takes the tool as Puff floats free.
Not yet. LOOK GEAR for the bent tooth and TALK TESS so she can stop and lock the machine first.
Tess says: We can do it together. LOOK GEAR, then TALK TESS before using the mallet.
Puff needs room to float, not a present. Fixing the jam will help him most.
The gear is part of the machine. It needs a repair, not a new owner.
Tess laughs. She is already on your team; there is no need to give her away.
You ask the gear to straighten up. It needs a little mechanical help.
You tell the mallet your plan. It looks ready for one gentle tap.
You cannot pick up a cloud with tongs. Puff wiggles his misty nose.
The tongs cannot straighten that gear tooth. Use the guide and ask Tess for help.
Cloud Care shows the blue gear tooth. LOOK GEAR, then ask Tess to stop the machine.
Cloud Care explains that a stuck machine can squash a cloud. Open its hatch by repairing the gear.
The tongs helped with the lamp and stairs. The mallet is the tool for this job.
The guide says: Find the bent tooth, stop the machine with a grown-up, then tap gently.
Your pinwheel note started a very useful team. Tess gives you an encouraging nod.

default: Puff puffs out his cheeks.
Tess keeps an eye on the controls.
The blue paint on the gear is easy to spot.
A tiny rainbow curls inside the chamber.
hints: Find the bent blue tooth. Ask Tess to stop the machine.
LOOK GEAR and TALK TESS. Then use the MALLET for one gentle tap.
LOOK GEAR, TALK TESS, then MALLET GEAR.

text: The gear clicks into place. The hatch opens.
Puff floats out, as soft as a pillow.
At last, the breeze is gentle enough for kites.

commands.response: Tess says: You noticed the clue and asked for help. That is how a good repair team works!
Puff says: Thank you! I can stretch again. Would you like a breeze for your kite?
Tess wipes her hands on her yellow apron. All three pencils are still behind her ear.
Puff stretches into a long cloud sausage, then curls into a happy ball.
You and Tess walk toward home and the kite fair. Puff drifts along overhead.
Tess offers a high five. Her glove makes a tiny puff of chalk dust.
You wave to Puff. He makes a little misty hand and waves back.
You tell the others about the kite plans on your desk. Puff wants to see them.
Home is just beyond the fair. Mom will be waiting there to hear the story.
You use the tongs to rescue a pencil from Tess's apron pocket. She laughs: Found it!
Tess says you may keep borrowing the tongs for your next project, with a grown-up.
Cloud Care helped you make a safe repair. Tess will return it to the library.
The note has a new crease. Quite a lot happened after that little TAP!

default: Puff practices a very gentle breeze.
Tess puts a tool back on its hook.
A kite outside begins to lift.
Your team smiles at its careful work.
hints: Puff is free! You can talk before heading back.
Mom is waiting to hear about your repair team.
GO HOME.

text: Mom meets you at the kite fair.
Puff makes a little cloud shaped like a sock.
Every kite lifts into the breeze.
You helped make room for a new friend.

commands.response: Tess adjusts a kite tail. She is very good at untangling things.
Tess says: Next time the town needs a careful helper, I know whom to ask.
Kites drift over the houses. A cloud-shaped kite is following a kite-shaped cloud.
You cheer for the kite fair. The baker waves a bun in celebration.
Mom listens as you explain the gear repair. She is glad you worked with Tess.
You are home beside Mom, with the kite fair just outside. A good place to finish.
You tuck the pinwheel note beside your kite plans. A keepsake from your repair team.
The tongs rest on your craft table, ready for another project with a grown-up.
Tess has marked the page she will show other helpers. She will return the book next.

default: Puff makes a cloud shaped like a sock.
Mom helps untangle your kite string.
Tess waves from the fair.
The breeze is just right.
